text.p: Brunswick Corp said Monday it plans to acquire additional active recreation businesses and will continue its internal focus on marketing.

"We will continue to emphasize aggressive marketing programs and innovative product introductions to increase sales in each of our business segments, and to acquire active recreation businesses to supplement internally-driven growth," chairman and chief executive Peter Larson said in a statement.
Brunswick's focus has been to build its active recreation business, and the company has acquired Igloo coolers, Mongoose bicycles, and Hoppe's hunting accessories.

"As a result of these actions, our marine operations are expected to grow, but at a slower rate than our other business units. Over time, marine segment sales are targeted to represent about half of total sales, compared with 68 percent in the first quarter and about 75 percent historically," Larson said.
Brunswick reported first quarter net earnings of $0.53 a share versus $0.46 a share last year. Sales were up nearly 13.9 percent at $841.6 million versus $738.9 million.
Recreation segment sales rose 42 percent to $273.0 million, and marine segment sales climbed four percent to $568.6 million.
Brunswick provides consumer products to both the indoor and outdoor active recreation and marine markets.
